## 固定收益開篇主論

中東石油運輸路線再受威脅，強化通膨風險；英國公債又大幅下跌，推高全球投資人持有長天期債券的報酬門檻。美國公債殖利率7月20日因而全線上升，2年期上升2.9個基點至4.209%，5年期上升4.3個基點至4.322%，10年期上升4.4個基點至4.593%，30年期則上升4.2個基點至5.113%。

這不只是短端因聯準會利率預期而調整。10年期實質殖利率上升3.3個基點至2.328%，10年期損益兩平通膨率也上升1.1個基點至2.265%，顯示投資人同時要求更高的通膨調整後報酬與略高的通膨補償。2年與10年期利差擴大1.5個基點至38.4個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大1.3個基點至90.4個基點；長端殖利率上升，但曲線並未明顯失序。

油價構成美國眼前的通膨疑慮。美國與伊朗持續相互攻擊，伊朗支持的胡塞武裝又威脅封鎖沙烏地阿拉伯在紅海的海運交通，WTI上漲0.90%至$83.23，布蘭特原油上漲1.27%至$89.22。荷莫茲海峽航運仍近乎停滯，沙烏地阿拉伯因而更加依賴紅海路線。調停方案促使原油自盤中高點回落，卻未消除干擾由一條主要出口航線蔓延至另一條的可能性。

英國局勢也影響債市反應。新任首相Andy Burnham表示，將運用現有財政規則所容許的彈性為投資籌措資金，令原已對公共借款敏感的市場不安。英國10年期公債殖利率收高8個基點至5.03%，30年期上升9個基點至5.75%，創5月20日以來最高。英國公債表現遜於美債與歐元區政府債券，英鎊也在談話後走弱。

這一交易日強化了聯準會耐心觀望的理由，卻不足以支持殖利率下行。市場仍認為7月會議升息的可能性很低；DoubleLine則主張，偏高的市場殖利率已收緊金融條件，若通膨繼續降溫，官員可以維持政策利率不變。然而，市場仍反映年底前將收緊0.34個百分點。油價轉強、全球期限殖利率上升，以及美國通膨風險尚未化解，使後續升息路徑依然存在。

信用市場呈現分化，並非普遍受損。投資人重新評估AI投資背後的債務負擔，Oracle的違約保護成本升至2008年以來資料中的最高水準。與此同時，BlackRock正為Meta相關的德州資料中心籌備超過$120億的債券融資，Netflix重返投資等級市場籌資$10億，印度一筆大型私人信貸再融資也以兩位數殖利率成交。市場的差別不是融資管道開放或關閉，而是借款人雖仍能取得資金，所面對的價格、結構與交易完成風險卻愈來愈取決於個別發行人。

## 油價壓力超越原油基準

儘管基準原油收盤低於盤中高點，能源衝擊仍在7月20日擴大。美國軍人遇害後，美軍連續第9天空襲伊朗，伊朗也繼續攻擊美國在區內的據點。美國總統Donald Trump表示，德黑蘭將為美軍死亡付出代價；伊朗官員則稱，調停者已提出終止衝突的方案。

胡塞武裝的威脅把另一條供應路線納入風險範圍。該組織稱，為回應沙烏地阿拉伯圍困葉門首都，將立即封鎖來自沙烏地阿拉伯的海運交通。沙烏地阿拉伯表示，將採取必要措施保護本國船隻。荷莫茲海峽航運受到嚴重限制之際，紅海路線讓沙國得以透過橫跨國土的輸油管與延布港，每日輸出數百萬桶石油。

沙烏地阿拉伯6月經延布出口的石油達每日419萬桶，創歷史新高。在戰前承擔全球約五分之一石油運輸量的荷莫茲海峽受阻後，這股流量一直是重要緩衝。因此，紅海若確實受到限制，影響並非只是重複原油價格已反映的風險，而是削弱最主要繞道出口路線的效用。

WTI收於$83.23，一週上漲6.51%；布蘭特原油收於$89.22，一週漲幅達7.11%。相較於地緣政治消息的嚴重程度，單日漲幅仍屬溫和，原因是調停報導提供了可能的降溫途徑。不過，油價仍延續反彈；此前公布的6月通膨數據曾受惠於能源價格下跌。

更棘手的通膨訊號來自成品油。衡量原油轉化為汽油與柴油利潤的3-2-1裂解價差升至約$70，超過歷史平均值的6倍。美國平均汽油價格約為每加侖$4.60，高於一年前同期的$3.63。成品油與原油走勢的落差顯示，只觀察原油價格會低估家庭與高度依賴運輸的企業實際承受的壓力。

目前的限制在於煉油產能與成品油供應，而不是全球原油絕對短缺。中國為穩定原油價格而增加庫存，卻同時減少汽油與柴油出口，使成品油市場更為緊張；烏克蘭攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠又增添一項干擾。釋出戰略原油可以補充煉油原料，但無法迅速取代受損的煉油產能或恢復成品油出口。

Ryanair的季度業績顯示這項衝擊如何傳導至企業。稅後獲利由€8.2億下降34%至€5.38億，低於分析師預估的約€6.24億。公司表示，中東衝突推高油料成本、削弱需求，旅客也因擔心航空燃油短缺而延後訂票。Ryanair在夏季旺季降價刺激需求，並表示會計年度第2季票價略低於一年前。

Ryanair已按每桶$67的價格鎖定至明年3月所需航空燃油的80%，但其餘20%仍使全年單位成本暴露於目前市況。今年前3個月，未避險部分的燃油費用增加逾一倍，單位成本與營運成本均已上升。即使飛機短缺限制全產業運能，公司仍因下半年能見度有限而未提供全年獲利指引。

這些細節顯示，能源價格上升未必只會帶來更強的通膨與更緊的政策。短期內，能源衝擊會推高整體物價與企業成本，但隨之而來的需求損害也可能削弱成長；Ryanair同時面對投入成本增加與訂票轉弱。就美債市場而言，目前證據尚不足以讓成長衝擊成為主導因素。實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步上升，反映投資人提高持有利率部位所要求的報酬，而非主要把能源衝擊視為未來寬鬆的理由。

貨幣市場的動向則顯示，政策不確定性如何影響配置最短天期資產的投資人。管理超過$8兆資產的基金偏好數週內到期、續作或重設利率的工具，以降低即使不大的利率風險，並保留殖利率上升後重新投資的能力。最初的油價衝擊與聯準會主席Kevin Warsh的鷹派語調一度令市場預期7月可能升息，但溫和的通膨數據隨後使近期收緊預期大幅下降，促成這項配置轉變。

DoubleLine對同一輪市場收緊提出不同解讀。該公司全球主權債與新興市場資產經理Bill Campbell認為，美債殖利率偏高已在推升借款成本，可以代替聯準會完成部分緊縮工作。依此觀點，Warsh強調讓通膨回到2%，已充分恢復政策可信度；只要通膨繼續降溫，官員便可按兵不動。

但這項判斷有重要前提。Campbell認為無須升息，是以通膨不再出現意外為條件，而油價衝擊使這項條件更難判斷。他也主張，貨幣政策無法直接逆轉供給衝擊，聯準會應保持耐心。市場只接受了部分論點：7月升息風險大致消退，但今年稍後仍保留相當幅度的緊縮定價。

跨資產交易謹慎，卻未失序。標普500指數下跌0.19%，Nasdaq 100小漲0.04%；費城半導體指數在前一週進入熊市後反彈0.60%，但一週仍下跌4.89%，一個月跌幅達18.11%。美元指數上漲0.24%至100.99。即使軍事衝突升級，金價仍大致持平於$4,010.30，因預期政策利率升高持續與無息黃金的地緣政治避險需求相互抗衡。

美債交易活動增加，但不代表資金單向流動。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$8,284億，共306,778筆，較7月17日增加9.1%；名目附息債券交易量增加2%至$6,228億。超過5年、但不超過7年的券種交易量激增78.8%至$608億；超過2年、但不超過3年的券種則增加33.5%至$836億。這些活動數據包含雙向交易，但交易集中的位置符合當日市場同時重新評估政策時程與中期債券持有成本的情況。

## Burnham的財政彈性遭遇英國公債市場界線

英國公債是當日表現最弱的主權債券。Burnham就任首相首日承諾建立新的經濟模式並終結政治不穩定，市場焦點卻落在他打算運用現有財政架構內的彈性。投資人擔心，新政府即使形式上遵守規則，實際借款負擔仍可能增加。

Burnham一再強調政府將保留現行規則，並會說明預算如何籌資。他把可能運用的彈性與增加基礎建設投資相連，也表示自己過去擔任公職時一向審慎。不過，這些保證仍未回答相關計畫會增加多少債務、或有曝險與利息成本。

討論中的選項之一，是讓National Wealth Fund等公共金融機構擴大借款。Resolution Foundation提議向該基金注資£160億，希望吸引逾£400億私人資金共同投資能源與基礎建設。這類機構的借款可置於政府主要債務規則之外；該規則要求公共部門淨金融負債相對GDP的比率，須在國會預測期結束前下降。

但會計處理方式不會消除融資成本。Resolution估計，每增加£10億借款，每年利息支出約增加£5,000萬。市場疑慮正源於這項差別：投資可以不計入某項規則，政府卻仍須籌得資金並償付債務。投資人檢視的是計畫的經濟實質，而不只是技術上是否符合規定。

Burnham也表示，正考慮把免稅個人扣除額由£12,750上調，這將是5年來首次，但他承認成本高昂。他承諾改革社會照護制度，並稱詳細支出計畫將隨預算案公布。各項政策或許各有理由，合併來看卻提高了完整融資計畫的重要性，也使支出能否符合財政護欄所採用的假設更受關注。

英國10年期公債殖利率收於5.03%，上升8個基點；30年期升至5.75%，上升9個基點，創5月底以來最高。長端表現較差，顯示市場要求的是財政風險與期限風險補償，而不只是調整對英格蘭銀行利率路徑的預期。英鎊下跌也支持這項解讀。

英國進入政權交接時，借款成本已是G10最高，公共債務規模也約等於一年的經濟產出，因此Burnham的措辭格外重要。市場並非反對所有以借款支持的投資，而是要求政府以專案報酬、可信的限制及完整債息試算，證明生產性投資與財政紀律鬆弛之間確有區別。

11月預算案將提供更完整的檢驗，但首日的拋售顯示，投資人不願被動等待細節。政府的長期經濟計畫要到今年稍後才會公布；在此之前，每項支出提案、機構融資工具與稅制調整，都將接受英國公債殖利率曲線所顯示融資成本的檢驗。

英國行情也影響境外市場。美債跟隨英國公債部分跌勢，全球債券投資人再次看到財政政策如何提高長天期政府債務所需的殖利率。美債拋售另有油價與聯準會因素，但兩地同時重新定價，降低了美債僅憑地緣政治風險上漲的空間。

## AI融資擴大取得資金與定價之間的落差

Oracle出現最明顯的個別發行人信用惡化。5年期信用違約交換年化成本週一早盤升至約203個基點，不僅高於週五的前高198.23個基點，也是2008年底以來資料中的最高水準。公司各期限現券同步走弱：2056年到期、票息6.7%的債券利差擴大約8個基點至263個基點；2036年到期、票息5.7%的債券利差則擴大約9個基點至205個基點。

在此之前，標普全球評級7月稍早以Oracle的AI支出規模為由，把公司評級調降至僅高於非投資等級一級。Moody’s給予Oracle Baa2評級，展望為負向。Morgan Stanley分析師Lindsay Tyler表示，Oracle仍可採取發行股票及要求客戶預付款等措施，因此不會立即降至高收益等級；但中期結果取決於投資計畫能否順利執行並變現。

Oracle是Bloomberg美國高評級公司債指數中最大的非金融業借款人，因而成為格外醒目的AI信用風險指標。其利差擴大本身並不足以證明科技業信用全面退潮，卻顯示債券持有人愈來愈重視時間落差：資料中心支出先行，AI合約帶來的預期現金流則較晚才會實現。

一款新的中國AI模型又加深市場疑慮，即科技領先地位與定價能力可能不如支出計畫所假設般持久。信用問題不只在於AI需求是否存在，而在於未來收入能否足夠迅速且穩定地實現，支撐企業在收入到來前為建置運算能力、電力基礎設施與資料中心而累積的債務。

一筆規模更大的潛在融資將檢驗這項問題。BlackRock計畫為Meta位於德州El Paso的資料中心園區發行超過$120億債券。發行人是一家持有BlackRock在Project Sopaipilla Holdings中80%權益的控股公司，Meta持有其餘20%。JPMorgan與Morgan Stanley預定週三安排投資人電話會議，定價預計在次週初進行。

BlackRock旗下Global Infrastructure Management與HPS Investment Partners所管理的基金持有多數股權。先前消息顯示，融資總額接近$130億。專案預計2028年開始營運，完工後將提供逾300個現場職位。

這項安排延續Meta以合資架構推動大型資料中心專案的作法。路易斯安那州另一項開發案採取Meta與Blue Owl Capital各持80%與20%的合資架構，並由$270億債務支持，使Meta能保留營運控制權，同時不把合資事業借款列在自身資產負債表上。Meta後來又把該據點擴展至合夥範圍之外，使估計開發成本升至$500億。

德州債券發行計畫提出之際，Amazon一筆$250億融資剛遭投資人冷淡回應，科技債市場也已吸收大幅增加的供給。因此，El Paso交易檢驗的不只是市場對Meta曝險的需求。投資人還須為控股公司架構、專案執行、Meta合約參與的價值與持久性，以及市場未來還要吸收多少AI相關長天期債券供給定價。

Netflix以較小規模取得融資。公司重返美國投資等級債市，發行$10億、2036年到期的債券，初步討論利差為美債加95個基點。募集資金計畫用於償還今年稍後到期的約$10億債務，以及一般公司用途。

這筆再融資推出之際，預期銷售成長放緩，加上收購Warner Bros. Discovery失敗，使市場更加檢視Netflix的成長動能。公司股價在此前一年約下跌46%；2056年到期債券週一盤中價格約為每$1面額報$0.9294，創一年盤中新低。這樣的背景有別於Netflix在2024年首次進入投資等級市場時的情況；當時$18億發債所獲需求超過發行額10倍。

Oracle、Meta相關專案與Netflix之間的差異，反映高評級債券投資組合正納入多種不同風險。Oracle積極推動資本支出，面對資產負債表與評級壓力；BlackRock交易把專案及結構風險集中於一筆極大型融資；Netflix則在股價與成長背景轉弱之際，為近期到期債務再融資。三者都能取得機構資金，但適用利差已不能單憑投資等級標籤決定。

大型交易在公開高評級市場之外也能成交，但殖利率高得多。印度Shapoorji Pallonji Group透過3年期零息盧比債券，完成約1,510億盧比、相當於$16億的私人信貸融資，定價殖利率為18.95%。參與者包括InCred Capital、DSP Finance及IIFL Capital等當地投資人，以及Farallon、Davidson Kempner與Cerberus等國際業者。

這筆資金將用於為Goswami Infratech的1,550億盧比債務再融資；該借款人先前已兩度延長到期日。集團另以殖利率14.5%的3年期美元債籌得$6.5億。目前交易是2,550億盧比籌資計畫的一部分，集團預計未來6個月再籌措$3.5億。

債務以Afcons Infrastructure與Tata Sons股票作為擔保。債權人部分仰賴集團把所持18.4%的Tata Sons股權變現；協議同時要求其在24個月內償還1,350億盧比。融資提供了即時流動性，但高殖利率、加速還款要求及對質押股權的依賴，仍留下可觀的執行風險。

巴西醫療服務業者Oncoclinicas提出另一種重整架構。IG4 Capital提議取得公司超過50%的表決權，既有股東則保留所持股份的經濟所有權。IG4若掌握表決控制權，便可直接參與營運與債務重整，無須立即進行傳統收購。

此前Oncoclinicas已與部分債權人就51億雷亞爾、約合$9.98億的債務達成庭外重整協議。IG4提議透過當地可轉換債券投入約5億雷亞爾新資金。只有在董事會給予IG4為期60天的盡職調查排他期後，該要約才具約束力，金額也可能在審查後調整。

新債券將取得類似債務人自行管理（DIP）融資的優先順位，但這項條款仍須與其他債權人協商。資金用途是維持營運並緩解藥品短缺。公司的整體重整還可能包括股東增資、把債權轉為股權或新債，以及修改攤還安排。因此，現階段只是有條件的紓困提案，並非已同意移轉控制權或完成最終債權人和解。

其他新融資的壓力較低，但仍會影響資產負債表。Magnolia Oil & Gas同意以含債務約$41億收購WildFire Energy。WildFire股東將取得3,220萬股Magnolia股票，Magnolia則將承接$6億、2029年到期的票據。交易預計第3季末完成，也是能源業在油價上升支撐下持續整併的另一案例。

## 歐洲與新興市場的借款成本不均上升

歐元區企業表示，第2季銀行信貸成本大幅上升。即使整體貸款供給大致穩定，這仍直接證明較高的政策利率與市場利率正在向企業傳導。淨42%的企業表示銀行貸款利率上升，高於第1季的26%；淨31%表示其他融資成本增加，另有10%面對更高的擔保品要求。

各類企業受到的影響並不一致。大型企業的銀行貸款可得性淨改善4%，中小企業則淨惡化4%。企業銀行貸款需求與可得性之間的融資缺口由2%擴大至3%。淨29%的受訪者表示整體經濟前景妨礙其取得外部融資，高於先前的26%。

ECB調查於5月21日至6月26日訪問5,087家企業，涵蓋中東衝突再起後企業的初步反應。企業預期未來12個月售價、非勞動投入成本及工資均會上升，但增速慢於前次調查；其通膨預期大致穩定。

企業進行AI投資時，對內部資金的偏好尤其明顯。計畫進行相關支出的企業中，72%預期使用內部資源；約16%分別提到銀行貸款、補助或租賃，只有1%預期使用債務證券。這些數字說明，少數科技公司的公開債券發行管線可以十分龐大，同時更廣泛企業部門對債市的使用仍然有限。

企業調查並不能證明銀行本身也以相同幅度收緊核准標準。ECB將於7月21日公布銀行放款調查，提供銀行端在放款標準、貸款需求及預期方面的證據。兩份調查合併觀察，將有助判斷借款成本上升主要只是價格效應，還是正演變成更廣泛的信貸供給限制。

印尼面對的是國內殖利率偏高、匯率防衛與油價曝險的另一種組合。印尼盾已由兌美元18,190的歷史低點回升約1.3%，上週五收盤接近17,895；3個月隱含波動率則由7.93%降至6.78%。Credit Agricole預測本季將朝17,850移動，Julius Baer預期第3季為17,800。

印尼央行今年已累計升息100個基點，並直接干預匯市支撐本幣。分析師對週三決策意見分歧，一方預期再升息25個基點，另一方則預期維持不變。這項分歧反映政策必須在維持印尼盾資產吸引力與避免進一步壓抑內需之間取捨。

印尼基準10年期政府債券殖利率約7.25%，在主要新興市場中名列前茅；外資可望連續第2個月成為淨買方。標普7月13日維持該主權的投資等級評級與展望。這些支撐減輕了眼前壓力，卻未消除油價上漲與能源補貼對財政的敏感度。

政府能否把赤字維持在GDP的3%以下，仍是重要的財政錨。印尼盾也面對股票市場重新分類引發資金外流的風險。Barclays估計，若MSCI把印尼降為邊境市場，可能引發約$150億被動賣盤。貨幣緊縮有助穩定匯率，卻無法單獨解決財政、經常帳或市場分類問題。

華盛頓特區則在市政債市場呈現信用觀感改善與供給龐大並存的局面。特區計畫週二發行$12億所得稅擔保債券，用於大眾運輸、學校、警務，以及前RFK Stadium場址重建相關基礎設施。

聯邦資金及就業遭削減後，Moody’s去年把特區評級由AAA調降至Aa1；今年4月則以財政治理與預算管理穩健為由，把展望由負向調升至穩定。市場對前Department of Government Efficiency的不確定性降低，有助穩定信用；華盛頓特區免稅債券供給有限，也可能支撐散戶需求。

然而，這筆債券將進入供給擁擠的市政債市場。今年迄今發行量約達$3,210億，比2025年同期增加4%；上半年約$2,950億的發行量更創10年新高。特區去年發行的10年期債券週一殖利率約3.3%。若投資組合既有曝險已高，或整體發行日程爭奪相同資金，投資人仍可能要求發行讓利。

## 前瞻市場意義

ECB第2季銀行放款調查將於7月21日10:00 CEST公布，這是檢驗歐元區企業所回報的成本上升是否伴隨銀行核准標準收緊或需求減弱的第一項直接測試。這項差異在ECB下次決策前相當重要：貸款利率上升、但未出現廣泛限貸，代表政策仍持續傳導；若標準收緊且需求轉弱，則會加重信貸已對成長形成的抑制。

印尼央行週三的決策將檢驗，累計100個基點的升息、匯市干預及外資需求改善，是否足以穩定印尼盾。若維持利率不變，政策將更仰賴既有緊縮效果與財政可信度；若再升息25個基點，則顯示匯率與能源補貼風險的重要性仍高於對內需承受更多壓力的憂慮。

美國財政部將於7月23日13:00 ET標售$210億新發10年期TIPS；實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率同步上升後，這將最直接檢驗市場對存續期的需求。債券將於7月31日交割，並於2036年7月15日到期。在原油與成品油壓力仍使通膨前景不明之際，投標需求將顯示2.328%的10年期實質殖利率是否足以吸引買方。

信用投資人同時面對多項交易測試。BlackRock將於週三開始為Meta相關的El Paso資料中心舉行投資人電話會議，預計次週初定價。在科技債券表現轉弱後，這筆交易的規模與結構將顯示另一項大型AI基礎設施融資需要多少利差。Netflix的最終定價及次級市場交易，則會顯示在企業成長敘事轉弱時，較傳統的再融資能以多大難度完成。

華盛頓特區$12億市政債預計7月21日定價。結果將區分Aa1評級展望穩定及當地免稅債券稀缺所帶來的好處，與市政債發行量創紀錄造成的壓力。訂單深度及所需發行讓利，會比名目發行額提供更多資訊。

日本6月全國消費者物價指數將於7月24日08:30 JST公布。進口能源成本上升、政策利率為1%之際，數據將影響市場對日本央行下一次政策調整的預期。關鍵在於，即使油價衝擊會損害成長，日本國內通膨是否仍足夠廣泛，足以支持進一步政策正常化。

英國6月零售銷售將於7月24日07:00 BST公布。在英國公債重新計入財政溢價之際，數據將顯示家庭需求還能承受多少壓力。消費強勁會縮小英格蘭銀行忽略輸入型通膨的空間；若數據疲弱，則在新政府擬定預算之際，金融條件收緊的代價將更加明顯。

美國7月24日10:00 ET將公布新屋銷售。這項數據將檢驗最直接暴露於高檔美債殖利率與房貸利率的產業之一，其需求表現如何。更廣泛的政策問題是，在油價壓力擴散為基礎通膨之前，偏高的市場借款成本是否已足以拖慢經濟活動，取代聯準會另一次升息。

固定收益市場的核心考驗，如今分成已實現的緊縮效果與未來價格風險兩端。美債殖利率、企業融資成本、英國公債借款利率及歐元區貸款成本，都在傳導更緊的金融條件；同時，荷莫茲海峽與紅海周邊的干擾正推升能源和成品油成本。若對信貸敏感的經濟活動轉弱、能源價格趨於穩定，偏高的實質殖利率可能開始吸引債券買盤。若航線干擾持續，企業也繼續為大型投資計畫籌資，市場就必須同時吸收更高的通膨風險與更多成本昂貴的債務供給。

overall_summary.headline: 石油航線受威脅、英國公債遭拋售，推高全球存續期報酬門檻與美債殖利率
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債殖利率全線上升：2年期上升2.9個基點至4.209%，5年期上升4.3個基點至4.322%，10年期上升4.4個基點至4.593%，30年期上升4.2個基點至5.113%。10年期實質殖利率增加3.3個基點至2.328%，10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1.1個基點至2.265%，顯示投資人同時要求更高的通膨調整後報酬與略高的通膨補償。

油價帶來眼前的通膨疑慮。美國與伊朗再度互相攻擊，胡塞武裝又威脅封鎖沙烏地阿拉伯在紅海的海運交通，使干擾可能由荷莫茲海峽向外擴散；WTI收於$83.23，布蘭特原油收於$89.22。調停消息令油價自盤中高點回落，卻未消除沙國主要繞道出口路線所受的威脅；異常偏高的煉油利潤與汽油價格，也顯示壓力已超越原油基準。

英國又增添一項全球利率衝擊。首相Andy Burnham計畫運用現有財政規則所容許的彈性，令投資人不安；英國10年期公債殖利率上升8個基點至5.03%，30年期上升9個基點至5.75%，英鎊同步走弱。市場認為聯準會7月升息的可能性很低，但仍反映年底前將收緊0.34個百分點。信用融資管道依然開放，不過Oracle的信用保護成本創新高，加上大型AI相關融資陸續推出，顯示價格、結構與交易完成風險正日益取決於個別發行人。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off across the curve on July 20 as renewed threats to Middle East oil routes reinforced inflation risk and a sharp decline in UK government bonds raised the global hurdle for owning duration. The 2-year yield rose 2.9 basis points to 4.209%, the 5-year increased 4.3 basis points to 4.322%, the 10-year climbed 4.4 basis points to 4.593%, and the 30-year added 4.2 basis points to 5.113%.

The move was more than a front-end adjustment to Federal Reserve expectations. The 10-year real yield increased 3.3 basis points to 2.328%, while the 10-year breakeven inflation rate rose 1.1 basis points to 2.265%. Investors demanded more inflation-adjusted return as well as slightly more inflation compensation. The 2s10s curve steepened 1.5 basis points to 38.4 basis points and 2s30s widened 1.3 basis points to 90.4 basis points, leaving long yields higher without a pronounced curve dislocation.

Oil supplied the immediate U.S. inflation concern. WTI rose 0.90% to $83.23 and Brent gained 1.27% to $89.22 after the United States and Iran extended their exchange of attacks and Tehran-backed Houthi militants threatened to blockade Saudi Arabian maritime traffic in the Red Sea. The threat matters because Saudi Arabia has relied more heavily on the Red Sea route while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains near a standstill. Mediation proposals helped crude retreat from earlier highs, but they did not remove the possibility that disruption could spread from one major export route to another.

The bond response was also shaped by developments in Britain. New Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would use available flexibility within existing fiscal rules to fund investment, unsettling a market already sensitive to public borrowing. The UK 10-year yield closed 8 basis points higher at 5.03%, while the 30-year rose 9 basis points to 5.75%, its highest level since May 20. Gilts underperformed both Treasuries and euro-area government debt, and sterling weakened after the remarks.

The session therefore strengthened the case for Federal Reserve patience without making the case for lower yields. Market pricing continued to assign little likelihood to an increase at the July meeting, and DoubleLine argued that the tightening delivered by elevated market yields could allow officials to leave the policy rate unchanged if inflation continues to moderate. Yet 0.34 percentage point of tightening remained priced by year-end. The combination of firmer oil, higher global term yields and unresolved U.S. inflation risk kept that later path alive.

Credit remained differentiated rather than broadly impaired. Oracle’s default-protection cost reached its highest level in data extending to 2008 as investors reassessed the debt burden behind artificial-intelligence investment. At the same time, BlackRock prepared a bond financing of more than $12 billion for a Meta-linked Texas data center, Netflix returned to the investment-grade market for $1 billion, and a large Indian private-credit refinancing closed at double-digit yields. The contrast was not between an open and a closed market. It was between borrowers able to obtain funding and the increasingly issuer-specific price, structure and execution risk attached to that funding.

## Oil Pressure Reaches Beyond the Crude Benchmark

The energy shock widened on July 20 even though benchmark crude finished below its intraday highs. U.S. forces carried out a ninth consecutive day of strikes on Iran after American service members were killed, while Iran continued attacks on U.S. positions in the region. President Donald Trump said Tehran would pay for the deaths, even as Iranian officials said mediators had brought forward proposals for ending the conflict.

The Houthi threat added a separate supply route to the risk map. The group said it would block maritime traffic from Saudi Arabia in response to the Saudi siege of Yemen’s capital and indicated that the action would take effect immediately. Saudi Arabia said it would take the measures necessary to protect its vessels. The Red Sea route has allowed the kingdom to move millions of barrels a day through its cross-country pipeline and the port of Yanbu while Hormuz traffic has been heavily restricted.

Saudi exports through Yanbu reached a record 4.19 million barrels a day in June. That flow has been an important buffer against the disruption around Hormuz, which carried about one-fifth of global oil before the war. A credible restriction in the Red Sea would therefore reduce the usefulness of the principal bypass rather than simply duplicate the risk already embedded in crude prices.

WTI’s close at $83.23 left it 6.51% higher over a week, while Brent’s $89.22 settlement represented a 7.11% weekly increase. The daily gains were moderate compared with the scale of the geopolitical headlines because reports of mediation offered a possible route toward de-escalation. They nevertheless extended a rebound that came after June inflation data benefited from lower energy prices.

The more difficult inflation signal was in refined products. The 3-2-1 crack spread, a measure of the margin from converting crude into gasoline and diesel, reached about $70, more than 6 times its historical average. Average U.S. gasoline prices were around $4.60 a gallon, compared with $3.63 at the same time a year earlier. That divergence showed why crude alone understated the pressure reaching households and transport-intensive businesses.

The constraint was refining capacity and product availability rather than an outright global shortage of crude. China’s efforts to stabilize crude prices included drawing oil into inventories, but reduced Chinese exports of gasoline and diesel tightened the market for finished fuels. Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries added another disruption. Strategic crude releases can supplement feedstock, but they cannot quickly replace lost refining capacity or restore product exports.

Ryanair’s quarterly results supplied a corporate example of that transmission. Profit after tax fell 34% to €538 million from €820 million and missed analysts’ estimates of about €624 million. The airline said the Middle East conflict raised oil costs, weakened demand and prompted later bookings amid concern about jet-fuel shortages. It cut fares to stimulate demand during the peak summer period and said fiscal second-quarter fares were modestly lower than a year earlier.

Ryanair has secured 80% of its jet-fuel needs through March at $67 a barrel, but the remaining 20% leaves its full-year unit costs exposed to the current market. Unit and operating costs already rose in the first 3 months of the year as the unhedged portion of its fuel bill more than doubled. The company withheld full-year profit guidance because visibility into the second half remained limited, even as aircraft shortages constrained industry capacity.

Those details complicate the simple assumption that higher energy prices necessarily produce only stronger inflation and tighter policy. The immediate effect raises headline prices and business costs, while the accompanying demand damage can weaken growth. Ryanair experienced both: a higher input bill and softer bookings. For the Treasury market, however, the current evidence was insufficient to make the growth effect dominant. Real yields rose alongside breakevens, showing that investors increased the required return on duration rather than treating the energy shock primarily as a reason for future easing.

Money-market behavior showed how policy uncertainty was affecting the shortest-duration investors. Funds overseeing more than $8 trillion were favoring assets that mature, roll over or reset within weeks, limiting exposure to even modest rate risk and preserving the ability to reinvest if yields rise. The shift followed a rapid swing from expectations of a possible July increase after the initial oil shock and Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish tone to much lower immediate tightening expectations after benign inflation releases.

DoubleLine offered a different interpretation of the same market tightening. Bill Campbell, who manages global sovereign and emerging-market assets at the firm, argued that high Treasury yields were already raising borrowing costs and could do part of the Fed’s work. On that view, Warsh’s emphasis on returning inflation to 2% has restored enough policy credibility for officials to remain on hold if inflation continues moderating.

The qualification is crucial. Campbell’s no-hike view was conditional on the absence of another inflation surprise, and the oil shock makes that condition harder to assess. He also argued that the Fed should be patient with a supply shock that monetary policy cannot directly reverse. Markets adopted only part of that logic: they removed most of the risk of a July increase but retained substantial tightening later in the year.

Cross-asset trading was cautious rather than disorderly. The S&P 500 fell 0.19%, while the Nasdaq 100 edged 0.04% higher and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 0.60% after entering bear-market territory the previous week. The semiconductor gauge remained 4.89% lower over a week and 18.11% lower over a month. The dollar index rose 0.24% to 100.99, while gold was nearly unchanged at $4,010.30 despite the military escalation. Higher prospective policy rates continued to compete with geopolitical demand for the non-yielding metal.

Treasury trading activity increased without indicating one-way investor flow. FINRA recorded $828.4 billion in par activity across 306,778 trades, 9.1% more than on July 17. Nominal-coupon activity rose 2% to $622.8 billion. Turnover in maturities longer than 5 years and no more than 7 years surged 78.8% to $60.8 billion, while the sector longer than 2 years and no more than 3 years increased 33.5% to $83.6 billion. The activity measures are two-way, but their concentration was consistent with a session in which both the policy horizon and the cost of intermediate duration were being reassessed.

## Burnham’s Fiscal Flexibility Meets a Gilt-Market Limit

Britain produced the clearest sovereign-bond underperformance of the session. Burnham used his first day as prime minister to promise a new economic model and an end to political instability, but markets focused on his intention to exploit flexibility within the existing fiscal framework. The remarks raised concern that the new government could comply formally with its rules while increasing the effective borrowing burden.

Burnham repeatedly said the government would retain the current rules and would explain how its budget was funded. He linked possible flexibility to greater infrastructure investment and said he had taken a prudent approach in previous offices. That reassurance did not settle the question of how much additional debt, contingent exposure or interest cost the program would create.

One option under discussion is to expand borrowing by public financial institutions such as the National Wealth Fund. The Resolution Foundation proposed a £16 billion capital injection into the fund, intended to attract more than £40 billion of private co-investment in energy and infrastructure. Borrowing by such institutions can sit outside the government’s principal debt rule, which requires public-sector net financial liabilities to fall relative to gross domestic product by the end of the parliamentary forecast horizon.

The accounting treatment does not eliminate the financing cost. Resolution estimated that each additional £1 billion of borrowing would add roughly £50 million in annual interest expense. That distinction drove the market’s concern: investment can be excluded from a particular rule, but the government still has to raise the money and service the debt. Investors were therefore testing the economic substance of the plan rather than only its technical compliance.

Burnham also said he was considering raising the tax-free personal allowance above £12,750 for the first time in 5 years, while acknowledging that such a change would be expensive. He pledged to reform social care and indicated that detailed spending plans would come with the budget. Each proposal may have a separate policy rationale, but together they increased the importance of the financing plan and the assumptions used to make it fit within the fiscal guardrails.

The 10-year gilt yield closed at 5.03%, up 8 basis points, while the 30-year reached 5.75%, up 9 basis points and at its highest since late May. The long end’s underperformance showed that the market was charging for fiscal and term risk rather than merely adjusting the expected path of the Bank of England. Sterling’s decline reinforced that interpretation.

Britain already entered the transition with the highest borrowing costs among the Group of 10 and public debt around the size of annual economic output. That made Burnham’s choice of language unusually consequential. The market was not rejecting all borrowing for investment; it was signaling that the distinction between productive investment and looser discipline must be demonstrated through project returns, credible limits and a complete debt-interest calculation.

The November budget will provide the fuller test, but the first-day selloff showed that investors were unwilling to wait passively for the details. The government’s longer-term economic plan is not due until later in the year. Between now and then, each spending proposal, institutional financing vehicle and tax change will be assessed against the cost of funding visible in the gilt curve.

The UK move also mattered outside Britain. Treasuries tracked part of the gilt decline, and global bond investors faced another example of fiscal policy increasing the required yield on long-duration government debt. The U.S. selloff had its own oil and Fed drivers, but the simultaneous repricing reduced the scope for Treasuries to rally on geopolitical risk alone.

## AI Financing Widens the Gap Between Access and Price

Oracle supplied the sharpest issuer-level credit deterioration. Five-year credit-default swaps rose to about 203 basis points annually early Monday, the highest level in data extending to the end of 2008 and above Friday’s previous peak of 198.23 basis points. The company’s cash bonds weakened across maturities: the spread on its 6.7% notes due in 2056 widened about 8 basis points to 263 basis points, while its 5.7% debt due in 2036 widened roughly 9 basis points to 205 basis points.

The move followed S&P Global Ratings’ decision earlier in July to lower Oracle to one notch above speculative grade, citing the scale of its AI spending. Moody’s rates the company Baa2 with a negative outlook. Morgan Stanley analyst Lindsay Tyler said a fall to high yield was not immediate because Oracle retains options including equity issuance and customer prepayments, but judged the medium-term outcome dependent on whether the investment program is executed and monetized successfully.

Oracle has become an especially visible measure of AI credit risk because it is the largest nonfinancial borrower in the Bloomberg U.S. high-grade corporate index. Its widening does not by itself establish a broad technology-credit retreat. It does show that bondholders are assigning increasing value to the timing mismatch between upfront data-center spending and the later cash flows expected from AI contracts.

A new Chinese AI model intensified the concern that technology leadership and pricing power may be less durable than the spending plans assume. The credit question is not simply whether AI demand exists. It is whether future revenue arrives quickly and predictably enough to support the debt accumulated to build computing capacity, power infrastructure and data centers before those revenues are realized.

That question will be tested by a much larger prospective financing. BlackRock plans to sell more than $12 billion of bonds for a Meta data-center campus in El Paso, Texas. The issuer is a holding company for BlackRock’s 80% interest in Project Sopaipilla Holdings; Meta owns the remaining 20%. JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley are due to arrange investor calls on Wednesday, with pricing expected early the following week.

Funds managed by BlackRock units Global Infrastructure Management and HPS Investment Partners hold the majority stake. Earlier indications had put total financing near $13 billion. The project is expected to begin operating in 2028 and support more than 300 on-site jobs when completed.

The structure extends Meta’s use of joint ventures for large data-center projects. A separate Louisiana development used an 80%-20% venture with Blue Owl Capital and was backed by $27 billion of debt, allowing Meta to retain operational control while keeping the venture’s borrowing away from its own balance sheet. Meta later expanded that site beyond the part covered by the partnership, taking estimated development cost to $50 billion.

The planned Texas sale arrives after investors gave a cool reception to Amazon’s $25 billion financing and after technology bonds broadly absorbed a large increase in supply. The El Paso transaction will therefore test more than demand for Meta exposure. Investors must price the holding-company structure, project execution, the value and durability of Meta’s contractual involvement, and the amount of additional AI-related duration likely to reach the market.

Netflix found access on a smaller scale. The company returned to the U.S. investment-grade market with $1 billion of notes due in 2036, initially discussed at a spread of 95 basis points over Treasuries. It plans to use the proceeds to repay about $1 billion of debt maturing later this year and for general corporate purposes.

The refinancing comes as slower expected sales growth and a failed effort to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery have increased scrutiny of Netflix’s momentum. Its shares were down about 46% over the preceding year, and its bonds due in 2056 traded at roughly 92.94 cents on the dollar on Monday, their lowest intraday price in a year. That backdrop distinguishes the new issue from Netflix’s investment-grade debut in 2024, when a $1.8 billion offering drew demand exceeding 10 times the amount sold.

The contrast among Oracle, the Meta-linked project and Netflix illustrates the range of risks entering high-grade portfolios. Oracle faces balance-sheet and rating pressure from an active capital-spending program. The BlackRock transaction concentrates project and structural exposure in a very large financing. Netflix is refinancing a near-term maturity against a weaker equity and growth backdrop. All can access institutional capital, but the relevant spread no longer follows from an investment-grade label alone.

Large transactions were also clearing outside public high-grade markets at much higher yields. India’s Shapoorji Pallonji Group completed a private-credit financing of about 151 billion rupees, or $1.6 billion, through 3-year zero-coupon rupee bonds priced to yield 18.95%. Local investors including InCred Capital, DSP Finance and IIFL Capital participated, alongside global firms including Farallon, Davidson Kempner and Cerberus.

The funds will refinance 155 billion rupees of debt at Goswami Infratech after the borrower twice extended its maturity. The group separately raised $650 million through a 3-year dollar bond at a 14.5% yield. The current transactions are part of a planned 255 billion-rupee funding program, and the group expects to seek another $350 million over the next 6 months.

The debt is backed by shares in Afcons Infrastructure and Tata Sons. Creditors are relying partly on the possibility that the group can monetize its 18.4% Tata Sons holding, while the agreement requires repayment of 135 billion rupees within 24 months. The financing provides immediate liquidity, but its high yield, accelerated repayment requirement and dependence on pledged equity leave substantial execution risk.

Brazilian medical provider Oncoclinicas presented a different restructuring structure. IG4 Capital proposed obtaining more than 50% of the company’s voting rights while existing shareholders retained the economic ownership of their shares. Voting control would allow IG4 to participate directly in operational and debt restructuring without requiring an immediate conventional takeover.

The proposal follows Oncoclinicas’ agreement with some creditors on an out-of-court restructuring of 5.1 billion reais, or about $998 million, of debt. IG4 offered approximately 500 million reais in fresh capital through local convertible bonds. The offer would become binding only if the board grants IG4 a 60-day exclusivity period for due diligence, and the amount could change after that review.

The new bonds would have priority similar to debtor-in-possession financing, a provision that still must be negotiated with other creditors. The money is intended to preserve operations and ease medicine shortages. The company’s broader restructuring could include shareholder capitalization, conversion of claims into equity or new debt, and revised amortization. The current development is therefore a conditional rescue proposal, not an agreed transfer of control or final creditor settlement.

Other new financing was less stressed but still relevant to balance sheets. Magnolia Oil & Gas agreed to acquire WildFire Energy for about $4.1 billion including debt. WildFire’s owners will receive 32.2 million Magnolia shares, while Magnolia will assume $600 million of notes due in 2029. The transaction is expected to close late in Q3 and adds another deal to an energy sector using higher crude prices to support consolidation.

## Borrowing Costs Tighten Unevenly Across Europe and Emerging Markets

Euro-area companies reported a sharp increase in the cost of bank credit during Q2, adding direct evidence that higher policy and market rates were passing through even though aggregate loan availability remained broadly stable. A net 42% of firms said bank-loan interest rates had increased, up from 26% in Q1. A net 31% reported higher other financing costs, while 10% faced greater collateral requirements.

The distribution was uneven. Bank-loan availability improved for large companies by a net 4% but declined for small and medium-sized enterprises by the same amount. The financing gap—the difference between firms’ need for bank loans and their availability—widened to 3% from 2%. A net 29% of respondents said the general economic outlook was constraining access to external finance, up from 26%.

The ECB survey covered 5,087 firms between May 21 and June 26, capturing the early corporate response to the renewed Middle East conflict. Companies expected selling prices, nonlabor input costs and wages to rise over the following 12 months, though at a slower pace than in the preceding survey. Their inflation expectations were broadly stable.

AI investment revealed a particularly strong preference for internal funding. Seventy-two percent of companies planning such spending expected to use internal resources. About 16% each cited bank loans, grants or leasing, while only 1% expected to use debt securities. The figures show why a large public bond pipeline from a small group of technology companies can coexist with limited debt-market use by the broader corporate sector.

The firm survey does not establish that banks themselves tightened approval standards by the same amount. The ECB’s bank lending survey on July 21 will provide the bank-side evidence on standards, loan demand and expectations. Together, the two releases will help determine whether the rise in borrowing costs is mainly a price effect or is becoming a broader restriction on credit availability.

Indonesia faced a different combination of high domestic yields, currency defense and oil exposure. The rupiah had recovered about 1.3% from its record low of 18,190 per dollar, ending Friday near 17,895, while 3-month implied volatility fell to 6.78% from 7.93%. Credit Agricole projected a move toward 17,850 this quarter, and Julius Baer expected 17,800 in Q3.

Bank Indonesia has raised its policy rate by a cumulative 100 basis points this year and used direct intervention to support the currency. Analysts were divided between another 25-basis-point increase and no change at Wednesday’s decision. That split captures the trade-off between preserving the appeal of rupiah assets and avoiding more restraint on domestic demand.

Indonesia’s benchmark 10-year government bond yielded about 7.25%, among the highest yields in major emerging markets, and foreign investors were on course to be net buyers for a second consecutive month. S&P retained the sovereign’s investment-grade rating and outlook on July 13. Those supports have reduced immediate pressure, but they do not remove the fiscal sensitivity to higher oil prices and energy subsidies.

The government’s ability to keep the deficit below 3% of gross domestic product remains an important anchor. The rupiah also faces the risk that an equity-market reclassification prompts capital outflows. Barclays estimated that a downgrade by MSCI to frontier status could generate about $15 billion in passive selling. Monetary tightening can help stabilize the currency, but it cannot by itself resolve fiscal, current-account or market-classification concerns.

Washington, DC offered a municipal version of the same balance between improved credit perception and heavy supply. The district plans to sell $1.2 billion of income-tax-backed bonds on Tuesday for transit, schools, policing and infrastructure associated with redevelopment of the former RFK Stadium site.

Moody’s lowered the district to Aa1 from AAA last year after federal funding and employment cuts, but revised the outlook to stable from negative in April, citing strong fiscal governance and budget management. Reduced uncertainty around the former Department of Government Efficiency has helped stabilize the credit, while limited availability of DC tax-exempt paper could support retail demand.

The sale nevertheless enters a crowded municipal calendar. Issuance reached about $321 billion so far this year, 4% more than in the comparable 2025 period, and first-half volume of roughly $295 billion was the largest in 10 years. Last year’s 10-year DC bonds yielded around 3.3% on Monday. Investors may still require concessions where portfolios already hold substantial exposure or where the broader supply calendar competes for the same cash.

## Forward Market Significance

The ECB’s Q2 bank lending survey, due July 21 at 10:00 CEST, is the first direct test of whether the higher costs reported by euro-area companies were accompanied by tighter bank approval standards or weaker demand. The distinction matters before the ECB’s next decision: a rise in loan rates without broad rationing would indicate continued transmission, while tighter standards and weaker demand would strengthen the growth restraint already operating through credit.

Bank Indonesia’s decision on Wednesday will test whether 100 basis points of tightening, intervention and improved foreign demand are sufficient to stabilize the rupiah. A hold would place more weight on existing restraint and fiscal credibility. Another 25-basis-point increase would show that currency and energy-subsidy risks still outweigh concern about additional pressure on domestic activity.

The U.S. Treasury’s $21 billion new 10-year TIPS auction on July 23 at 13:00 ET will provide the most direct duration test after both real yields and breakevens rose. The security settles July 31 and matures July 15, 2036. Demand will indicate whether a 2.328% 10-year real yield is sufficient to attract buyers while crude and refined-product pressure keep the inflation outlook unsettled.

Credit investors face several simultaneous execution tests. BlackRock’s investor calls for the Meta-linked El Paso data center begin Wednesday ahead of expected pricing early the following week. The transaction’s size and structure will show how much spread is required for another large AI infrastructure financing after weaker performance across technology debt. Netflix’s final pricing and secondary trading will show how readily a more conventional refinancing clears against a weakening corporate-growth narrative.

Washington’s $1.2 billion municipal sale is expected to price July 21. Its result will separate the benefit of a stabilized Aa1 outlook and scarce local tax-exempt paper from the pressure of record-scale municipal issuance. Order depth and any required concession will be more informative than the headline amount alone.

Japan’s June national consumer-price index arrives July 24 at 08:30 JST. It will shape expectations for the next Bank of Japan adjustment as imported energy costs rise and the policy rate stands at 1%. The release is especially important for whether domestic inflation remains broad enough to justify further normalization despite the growth cost of the oil shock.

UK retail sales for June are due July 24 at 07:00 BST. The data will show how much household demand can absorb while gilts carry a renewed fiscal premium. Strong consumption would leave the Bank of England with less room to look through imported inflation, while weakness would make the cost of tighter financial conditions more visible just as the new government develops its budget.

U.S. new-home sales follow at 10:00 ET on July 24. The release will test demand in one of the sectors most directly exposed to elevated Treasury and mortgage yields. The broader policy question is whether high market borrowing costs are slowing activity enough to substitute for another Fed increase before oil pressure broadens into underlying inflation.

The central fixed-income test is now divided between realized restraint and prospective price risk. Treasury yields, corporate funding costs, gilt borrowing rates and euro-area loan charges are all transmitting tighter financial conditions. At the same time, disruption around Hormuz and the Red Sea is lifting the cost of energy and refined products. If credit-sensitive activity weakens while energy prices stabilize, elevated real yields could begin to attract duration demand. If route disruptions persist and companies continue to fund large investment programs, the market will have to absorb both higher inflation risk and a larger supply of expensive debt.

section_summaries.section_title: Burnham’s Fiscal Flexibility Meets a Gilt-Market Limit
section_summaries.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham retained the UK fiscal rules but proposed using their flexibility to finance investment, including possible borrowing through public financial institutions. Markets focused on the economic debt and interest burden rather than formal accounting treatment: 10-year and 30-year gilt yields rose sharply, with the long end charging for fiscal and term risk as sterling weakened. Tax, social-care and infrastructure proposals increased the need for a complete financing plan.

section_summaries.section_title: AI Financing Widens the Gap Between Access and Price
section_summaries.summary: Oracle’s 5-year default protection reached about 203 basis points, its highest in data since 2008, as investors reassessed the debt burden and delayed cash flows behind AI spending. BlackRock’s planned $12 billion-plus Meta-linked data-center financing will test demand for a large holding-company structure after heavy technology issuance, while Netflix returned for a conventional $1 billion refinancing. Capital remained available, but pricing increasingly depended on balance sheets, structure and execution.

section_summaries.next_check: Bank Indonesia’s Wednesday decision will show whether existing tightening and intervention are sufficient to stabilize the rupiah.
section_summaries.section_title: Borrowing Costs Tighten Unevenly Across Europe and Emerging Markets
section_summaries.summary: A net 42% of euro-area firms reported higher bank-loan rates in Q2, but access improved for large companies and deteriorated for smaller firms, leaving the bank survey to determine whether higher prices are becoming broader credit restraint. Indonesia balanced currency support against domestic growth after 100 basis points of tightening, while oil subsidies and possible equity outflows remained risks. Washington’s improved credit outlook supported its $1.2 billion bond sale, although heavy municipal supply could require concessions.

Near-term tests will determine whether realized financial restraint or prospective inflation risk dominates. The ECB bank lending survey will separate higher loan prices from broader rationing, the 10-year TIPS auction will test demand after real yields and breakevens rose, and the Meta-linked financing will measure the concession required for another large AI project. Bank Indonesia, Japan’s CPI, UK retail sales and U.S. housing data will add evidence on how higher rates and energy costs are affecting currencies, inflation and growth.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury yields rise as oil-route threats and a gilt selloff raise the cost of duration
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasury yields rose across the curve, with the 2-year up 2.9 basis points to 4.209%, the 5-year up 4.3 basis points to 4.322%, the 10-year up 4.4 basis points to 4.593% and the 30-year up 4.2 basis points to 5.113%. The 10-year real yield increased 3.3 basis points to 2.328%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 1.1 basis points to 2.265%, showing that investors demanded more inflation-adjusted return as well as slightly more inflation compensation.

Oil supplied the immediate inflation concern. WTI closed at $83.23 and Brent at $89.22 after renewed U.S.-Iran attacks and a Houthi threat to block Saudi maritime traffic in the Red Sea raised the risk that disruption could spread beyond Hormuz. Mediation reports pulled crude below intraday highs but did not remove the threat to Saudi Arabia’s principal export bypass, while unusually elevated refining margins and gasoline prices showed pressure extending beyond crude benchmarks.

Britain added a global duration shock. Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s plan to use flexibility within existing fiscal rules unsettled investors, lifting the UK 10-year yield 8 basis points to 5.03% and the 30-year yield 9 basis points to 5.75% as sterling weakened. Markets retained little expectation of a July Fed increase but still priced 0.34 percentage point of tightening by year-end. Credit access remained open, although Oracle’s record protection cost and large AI-related financings showed that price, structure and execution risk were becoming more issuer-specific.
overall_summary.summary: Treasuries sold off across the curve as threats to Saudi Red Sea traffic extended the inflation risk beyond Hormuz and a UK fiscal repricing raised the global yield hurdle, while higher real yields showed investors demanding more compensation for duration rather than treating the oil shock mainly as a reason for future easing.
